{"parentUuid":"b60156c3-eb8a-48fb-bfc0-900096b61c1f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"e372a766-1a24-4c82-822f-cd4971523b5c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_014mrKePegrm7UExRs2gtMNa","type":"tool_result","content":"========\ntitle:\tSpec: Kenyon IR Office CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\nlabels:\tspec\ncomments:\t1\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. With multiple interns working at once, nobody can tell which version is current, and people outside the office resort to emailing IR directly to ask for the latest Factbook instead of finding it themselves.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — Director (admin) and Analyst (editor; each intern gets their own named account) — that separates draft from published content. Analysts can draft, edit, publish, and unpublish Data Bites (short, dated Markdown items) without waiting on the Director. Reports (Factbook, Common Data Set, Survey Policy) are Markdown pages, same as Data Bites, with an optional attached file (e.g. the actual Factbook PDF, when one exists) — matching how these documents actually circulate while keeping the core rubric's required Markdown-body field intact. Only the Director can publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it exists. `cms publish` exports only published content to a static public site on GitHub Pages, with content-type-namespaced paths.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a Director, I want to log in with a password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to log in with my own account, so that whichever intern is on shift can post routine content under their own name.\n3. As anyone, I want a wrong password rejected with a generic message, so that the login form doesn't reveal whether an account exists.\n4. As any authenticated user (Director or Analyst), I want to log out, so that a shared machine doesn't stay signed in.\n5. As a Director, I want to create a new user account (Director or Analyst), so that I can grant access as staffing changes.\n6. As a Director, I want to change a user's role, so that I can correct access if someone's responsibilities change.\n7. As a Director, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who's left the office can't log in anymore — even with a browser tab still holding an old session cookie — without deleting their history.\n8. As an Analyst, I want the admin console to hide user management entirely, so that I'm not tempted or able to touch accounts.\n9. As an Analyst, I want to create a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can post a survey result or announcement.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to save a Data Bite as a draft, so that I can work on it across multiple sessions before it's ready.\n11. As an Analyst, I want to publish a Data Bite myself, so that I don't have to wait on the Director for routine content.\n12. As an Analyst, I want to edit or unpublish a Data Bite (including one another Analyst drafted or published), so that shift changes don't block fixing a mistake.\n13. As a Director, I want to delete any Data Bite, so that outdated or wrong content can be fully removed; Analysts cannot delete Data Bites.\n14. As an Analyst, I want to create a **draft** Report (title, slug, Markdown body) and optionally attach a file (e.g. the Factbook PDF, when an official document exists), so that I can prepare the next cited document.\n15. As an Analyst, I want to edit a draft Report — its Markdown body, or the attached file — including one another Analyst started, so that shift changes don't block prep work.\n16. As an Analyst, I want to be unable to publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it's published, so that cited documents can't be changed or taken down without Director review.\n17. As a Director, I want to publish, edit (Markdown body or the attached file), or unpublish any Report, so that I control what's cited externally.\n18. As a Director, I want to delete any Report, so that outdated cited documents can be fully removed.\n19. As a Director or Analyst, I want a dashboard showing counts of Data Bites and Reports by status, so that I can see the state of the office's content at a glance.\n20. As a Director or Analyst, I want to filter the content list by type (Data Bite/Report) and status (draft/published), so that I can find something quickly.\n21. As a Director or Analyst, I want a Markdown preview while editing a Data Bite or a Report's caption, so that I can see how it will actually render (post-sanitization) before publishing.\n22. As a visitor, I want to see only published Data Bites and Reports on the public site, so that I never see draft or unreleased data, and never a draft's uploaded file.\n23. As a visitor, I want published Reports to appear in the public site's navigation, so that I can find the Factbook or Common Data Set without searching.\n24. As a visitor, I want to read a published Report's Markdown body on its page, and download its attached file if one exists, so that I get the full content plus the official document when available.\n25. As a Director, I want to run `cms publish` and have it regenerate `site/` from only published content, writing Data Bites to `data-bites/<slug>.html`, Reports to `reports/<slug>.html`, and Report files to `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>`, all with relative paths, so that the export works correctly on GitHub Pages and nothing collides.\n26. As an Analyst or Director, I want a duplicate slug within the same content type rejected at save time with a clear error, so that two items can never overwrite each other's export path.\n27. As an uploader, I want a Report's optional attached file restricted to an allowlisted file type (PDF) and a size cap, so that the upload path can't be used to smuggle arbitrary or oversized files.\n28. As anyone, I want content, files, and sessions to survive a server restart, so that nothing is lost between work sessions.\n29. As a security-conscious Director, I want passwords stored as argon2 hashes and every state-changing form — including login and logout — protected by a CSRF token, so that the office's accounts and content can't be trivially compromised.\n30. As a security-conscious Director, I want Markdown (Data Bite bodies, Report captions) stored raw and sanitized only at render time (preview and export), so that a pasted `<script>` tag can never execute anywhere it's displayed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: internal role values stay `admin` and `editor` (compatibility with `tests/conftest.py`'s `DEMO_USERS` and `client_as` fixture); templates display them as \"Director\" and \"Analyst\" respectively. No third role.\n- **DataBite**: title, slug, raw Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`.\n- **Report**: title, slug, required raw Markdown body (same shape as `DataBite`, satisfies core rubric C4), optional attached file (PDF; allowlisted extension + MIME type; size-capped — exact cap is an implementation detail, pick something generous but bounded, e.g. 20MB), status, author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`. The optional-file part doubles as the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal.\n- **Shift-continuity editing**: any Analyst may edit an item (Data Bite, or a Report while still draft) regardless of who created or last edited it; the original author and `created_at` are preserved, only `updated_at` changes.\n- **Permission rule** (ADR-003): Analysts — full create/edit/publish/unpublish on `DataBite`, no delete. Analysts — create/edit on **draft** `Report` only (Markdown body and/or the optional attached file); once a `Report` is published, only the Director may edit, unpublish, or delete it, and only the Director may ever publish one. Directors — full CRUD + publish on both, plus user management. Enforced server-side on every route — hiding a link is not access control (Security Checklist item 10).\n- **Auth**: every `/admin/*` route requires an authenticated session (redirect to login if anonymous). Every protected request re-validates the session's user as active server-side — a deactivated user's existing signed cookie must fail on the next request, not just on next login. Session via signed cookies (`itsdangerous`), password hashing via `argon2-cffi`.\n- **CSRF**: a per-session token embedded in every state-changing form and validated server-side on POST, including `/login` and `/logout`.\n- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: raw Markdown is what's stored (Data Bite bodies, Report captions). Rendering (preview or export) always runs `markdown-it-py` → `nh3` before display; pre-rendered/sanitized HTML is never persisted.\n- **File uploads (optional)**: handled via the existing `python-multipart` dependency (no new dependency needed). When present, the file is stored outside `site/` (e.g. a local `uploads/` directory, gitignored like the DB) until publish; a draft Report's file must never appear in `site/`, same rule as draft content generally. A Report with no attached file exports as a plain Markdown page, same as a Data Bite.\n- **Publish gate & export paths**: an item reaches `site/` only when `status == published`. `cms publish` (`app/publish.py`) writes published `DataBite` rows to `data-bites/<slug>.html`, published `Report` rows to `reports/<slug>.html` (rendering the Markdown body, plus a download link when a file is attached), and copies each published Report's attached file, if any, to `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>` — all relative paths. Namespacing by type means a Data Bite and a Report may share a slug; two items of the *same* type sharing a slug is rejected at save time with a form validation error.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only.\n- **Individual Analyst accounts** (ADR-003, reversed from an earlier shared-account draft): each intern gets their own named Analyst-role account, created and deactivated by the Director as rotations change. Shift continuity (any Analyst can edit any other Analyst's draft) is preserved as a permission rule, not by sharing a login — author and created_at are unaffected by who edits.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no isolated unit-testing of permission logic. `DEMO_USERS`/`client_as` keeps using `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` role keys (per the internal-role-values decision above); UI-label tests separately assert \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" appear in rendered admin templates.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state and exported-file assertions where relevant.\n- Access-control tests per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3. Includes a specific test that a deactivated user's still-valid-looking session cookie is rejected on the next request.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form (including login and logout) with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload in a Data Bite body and a Report body, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft Data Bite and a draft Report (with its file) present, assert both are absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n- Upload-validation test: a non-PDF or oversized attached file is rejected at upload time with a clear error; a Report with no attached file still publishes and exports correctly.\n- Slug-collision test: saving a second item of the same content type with an existing slug is rejected with a validation error, not a silent overwrite.\n- Published-Report lockdown test: an Analyst attempting to edit (Markdown body or attached file), unpublish, or delete an already-published Report is rejected, even though they could when it was a draft.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003), uploads for Data Bites (Data Bites stay Markdown-only; only Reports may optionally carry an attached file).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric, plus the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal folded into the Report content type. `/to-tickets` will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\n\n\n========\n# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Each intern gets their own named Analyst account (see\nADR-003). Can draft and publish Data Bites directly; can draft but not\npublish or edit Reports. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"ca013888-7fb1-4941-b2fa-aec3a6a70fac","timestamp":"2026-09-29T15:09:55.515Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"========\ntitle:\tSpec: Kenyon IR Office CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\nlabels:\tspec\ncomments:\t1\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon's Office of Institutional Research (Director + rotating student Analysts) currently publishes Data Bites and Reports by emailing files around and dropping them in a shared OneDrive folder. With multiple interns working at once, nobody can tell which version is current, and people outside the office resort to emailing IR directly to ask for the latest Factbook instead of finding it themselves.\n\n## Solution\n\nA CMS with two roles — Director (admin) and Analyst (editor; each intern gets their own named account) — that separates draft from published content. Analysts can draft, edit, publish, and unpublish Data Bites (short, dated Markdown items) without waiting on the Director. Reports (Factbook, Common Data Set, Survey Policy) are Markdown pages, same as Data Bites, with an optional attached file (e.g. the actual Factbook PDF, when one exists) — matching how these documents actually circulate while keeping the core rubric's required Markdown-body field intact. Only the Director can publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it exists. `cms publish` exports only published content to a static public site on GitHub Pages, with content-type-namespaced paths.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a Director, I want to log in with a password, so that I can access the admin console.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to log in with my own account, so that whichever intern is on shift can post routine content under their own name.\n3. As anyone, I want a wrong password rejected with a generic message, so that the login form doesn't reveal whether an account exists.\n4. As any authenticated user (Director or Analyst), I want to log out, so that a shared machine doesn't stay signed in.\n5. As a Director, I want to create a new user account (Director or Analyst), so that I can grant access as staffing changes.\n6. As a Director, I want to change a user's role, so that I can correct access if someone's responsibilities change.\n7. As a Director, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who's left the office can't log in anymore — even with a browser tab still holding an old session cookie — without deleting their history.\n8. As an Analyst, I want the admin console to hide user management entirely, so that I'm not tempted or able to touch accounts.\n9. As an Analyst, I want to create a Data Bite (title, slug, Markdown body), so that I can post a survey result or announcement.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to save a Data Bite as a draft, so that I can work on it across multiple sessions before it's ready.\n11. As an Analyst, I want to publish a Data Bite myself, so that I don't have to wait on the Director for routine content.\n12. As an Analyst, I want to edit or unpublish a Data Bite (including one another Analyst drafted or published), so that shift changes don't block fixing a mistake.\n13. As a Director, I want to delete any Data Bite, so that outdated or wrong content can be fully removed; Analysts cannot delete Data Bites.\n14. As an Analyst, I want to create a **draft** Report (title, slug, Markdown body) and optionally attach a file (e.g. the Factbook PDF, when an official document exists), so that I can prepare the next cited document.\n15. As an Analyst, I want to edit a draft Report — its Markdown body, or the attached file — including one another Analyst started, so that shift changes don't block prep work.\n16. As an Analyst, I want to be unable to publish, edit, unpublish, or delete a Report once it's published, so that cited documents can't be changed or taken down without Director review.\n17. As a Director, I want to publish, edit (Markdown body or the attached file), or unpublish any Report, so that I control what's cited externally.\n18. As a Director, I want to delete any Report, so that outdated cited documents can be fully removed.\n19. As a Director or Analyst, I want a dashboard showing counts of Data Bites and Reports by status, so that I can see the state of the office's content at a glance.\n20. As a Director or Analyst, I want to filter the content list by type (Data Bite/Report) and status (draft/published), so that I can find something quickly.\n21. As a Director or Analyst, I want a Markdown preview while editing a Data Bite or a Report's caption, so that I can see how it will actually render (post-sanitization) before publishing.\n22. As a visitor, I want to see only published Data Bites and Reports on the public site, so that I never see draft or unreleased data, and never a draft's uploaded file.\n23. As a visitor, I want published Reports to appear in the public site's navigation, so that I can find the Factbook or Common Data Set without searching.\n24. As a visitor, I want to read a published Report's Markdown body on its page, and download its attached file if one exists, so that I get the full content plus the official document when available.\n25. As a Director, I want to run `cms publish` and have it regenerate `site/` from only published content, writing Data Bites to `data-bites/<slug>.html`, Reports to `reports/<slug>.html`, and Report files to `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>`, all with relative paths, so that the export works correctly on GitHub Pages and nothing collides.\n26. As an Analyst or Director, I want a duplicate slug within the same content type rejected at save time with a clear error, so that two items can never overwrite each other's export path.\n27. As an uploader, I want a Report's optional attached file restricted to an allowlisted file type (PDF) and a size cap, so that the upload path can't be used to smuggle arbitrary or oversized files.\n28. As anyone, I want content, files, and sessions to survive a server restart, so that nothing is lost between work sessions.\n29. As a security-conscious Director, I want passwords stored as argon2 hashes and every state-changing form — including login and logout — protected by a CSRF token, so that the office's accounts and content can't be trivially compromised.\n30. As a security-conscious Director, I want Markdown (Data Bite bodies, Report captions) stored raw and sanitized only at render time (preview and export), so that a pasted `<script>` tag can never execute anywhere it's displayed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: internal role values stay `admin` and `editor` (compatibility with `tests/conftest.py`'s `DEMO_USERS` and `client_as` fixture); templates display them as \"Director\" and \"Analyst\" respectively. No third role.\n- **DataBite**: title, slug, raw Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`.\n- **Report**: title, slug, required raw Markdown body (same shape as `DataBite`, satisfies core rubric C4), optional attached file (PDF; allowlisted extension + MIME type; size-capped — exact cap is an implementation detail, pick something generous but bounded, e.g. 20MB), status, author reference, `created_at`/`updated_at`. The optional-file part doubles as the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal.\n- **Shift-continuity editing**: any Analyst may edit an item (Data Bite, or a Report while still draft) regardless of who created or last edited it; the original author and `created_at` are preserved, only `updated_at` changes.\n- **Permission rule** (ADR-003): Analysts — full create/edit/publish/unpublish on `DataBite`, no delete. Analysts — create/edit on **draft** `Report` only (Markdown body and/or the optional attached file); once a `Report` is published, only the Director may edit, unpublish, or delete it, and only the Director may ever publish one. Directors — full CRUD + publish on both, plus user management. Enforced server-side on every route — hiding a link is not access control (Security Checklist item 10).\n- **Auth**: every `/admin/*` route requires an authenticated session (redirect to login if anonymous). Every protected request re-validates the session's user as active server-side — a deactivated user's existing signed cookie must fail on the next request, not just on next login. Session via signed cookies (`itsdangerous`), password hashing via `argon2-cffi`.\n- **CSRF**: a per-session token embedded in every state-changing form and validated server-side on POST, including `/login` and `/logout`.\n- **Markdown/sanitization pipeline**: raw Markdown is what's stored (Data Bite bodies, Report captions). Rendering (preview or export) always runs `markdown-it-py` → `nh3` before display; pre-rendered/sanitized HTML is never persisted.\n- **File uploads (optional)**: handled via the existing `python-multipart` dependency (no new dependency needed). When present, the file is stored outside `site/` (e.g. a local `uploads/` directory, gitignored like the DB) until publish; a draft Report's file must never appear in `site/`, same rule as draft content generally. A Report with no attached file exports as a plain Markdown page, same as a Data Bite.\n- **Publish gate & export paths**: an item reaches `site/` only when `status == published`. `cms publish` (`app/publish.py`) writes published `DataBite` rows to `data-bites/<slug>.html`, published `Report` rows to `reports/<slug>.html` (rendering the Markdown body, plus a download link when a file is attached), and copies each published Report's attached file, if any, to `reports/files/<slug>.<ext>` — all relative paths. Namespacing by type means a Data Bite and a Report may share a slug; two items of the *same* type sharing a slug is rejected at save time with a form validation error.\n- **Navigation**: public nav is built from published `Report`s only.\n- **Individual Analyst accounts** (ADR-003, reversed from an earlier shared-account draft): each intern gets their own named Analyst-role account, created and deactivated by the Director as rotations change. Shift continuity (any Analyst can edit any other Analyst's draft) is preserved as a permission rule, not by sharing a login — author and created_at are unaffected by who edits.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- All tests exercise real HTTP behavior through `TestClient` via the existing `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py` — no isolated unit-testing of permission logic. `DEMO_USERS`/`client_as` keeps using `\"admin\"`/`\"editor\"` role keys (per the internal-role-values decision above); UI-label tests separately assert \"Director\"/\"Analyst\" appear in rendered admin templates.\n- Prior art: `tests/test_t00.py` — status-code and text-content assertions against real requests, extended with DB-state and exported-file assertions where relevant.\n- Access-control tests per route: every Director-only route rejects an Analyst session (403/redirect) and rejects an anonymous session (redirect to login) — Security Checklist items 4–5, rubric D3. Includes a specific test that a deactivated user's still-valid-looking session cookie is rejected on the next request.\n- CSRF tests: replay one POST per state-changing form (including login and logout) with the token stripped, expect rejection — Security Checklist item 3, rubric D2.\n- Sanitization test: save a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload in a Data Bite body and a Report body, publish, assert it's inert in both the admin preview and the exported HTML — Security Checklist item 7, rubric D4.\n- Draft-leak test: publish with a draft Data Bite and a draft Report (with its file) present, assert both are absent from `site/` — Security Checklist item 8.\n- Upload-validation test: a non-PDF or oversized attached file is rejected at upload time with a clear error; a Report with no attached file still publishes and exports correctly.\n- Slug-collision test: saving a second item of the same content type with an existing slug is rejected with a validation error, not a silent overwrite.\n- Published-Report lockdown test: an Analyst attempting to edit (Markdown body or attached file), unpublish, or delete an already-published Report is rejected, even though they could when it was a draft.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nPer the manual and rubric: multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. Also out of scope for the core spec (available separately as `stretch` tickets if pursued): categories/tags, revision history/rollback, scheduled publishing, site search, comments/moderation, a plugin/hook system, switchable themes, per-intern individual accounts (deliberately rejected, see ADR-003), uploads for Data Bites (Data Bites stay Markdown-only; only Reports may optionally carry an attached file).\n\n## Further Notes\n\nThis spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the rubric, plus the \"Media uploads\" stretch goal folded into the Report content type. `/to-tickets` will slice this into 7–9 vertical slices, each touching data model + route + template + test per rubric B3.\n\n\n========\n# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\n    21\tAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n    22\t_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n    23\t\n    24\t\n    25\tclass ContentError(ValueError):\n    26\t    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n    27\t\n    28\t\n    29\tclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n    30\t    pass\n    31\t\n    32\t\n    33\tdef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    34\t    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n    35\t    if not title:\n    36\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n    37\t    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n    38\t        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n    39\t                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n    40\t    if not body.strip():\n    41\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n    42\t    return title, slug, body\n    43\t\n    44\t\n    45\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n    46\tclass ContentTable:\n    47\t    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n    48\t    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n    49\t    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n    50\t    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n    51\t\n    52\t    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    53\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n    54\t            return conn.execute(\n    55\t                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n    56\t                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n    57\t                params,\n    58\t            ).fetchall()\n    59\t\n    60\t    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n    61\t        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n    62\t        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n    63\t            raise exc\n    64\t        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n    65\t\n    66\t    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n    67\t               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n    68\t        \"\"\"Create a draft.\"\"\"\n    69\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n    70\t        try:\n    71\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n    72\t                item_id = conn.execute(\n    73\t                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id)\"\n    74\t                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n    75\t                    (title, slug, body, author_id),\n    76\t                ).lastrowid\n    77\t                if also:\n    78\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n    79\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n    80\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n    81\t        return item_id\n    82\t\n    83\t    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n    84\t               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n    85\t        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. The author, created_at, and status are\n    86\t        kept. With drafts_only, a published item is left alone. False if\n    87\t        nothing was changed.\"\"\"\n    88\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n    89\t        try:\n    90\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n    91\t                changed = conn.execute(\n    92\t                    f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?,\"\n    93\t                    \" updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n    94\t                    \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n    95\t                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n    96\t                ).rowcount == 1\n    97\t                if changed and also:\n    98\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n    99\t                return changed\n   100\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n   101\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n   102\t\n   103\t    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n   104\t        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n   105\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n   106\t\n   107\t    def list_all(self) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   108\t        return self._select(\"1\", \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\")\n   109\t\n   110\t    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   111\t        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n   112\t\n   113\t    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n   114\t        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n   115\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   116\t            return conn.execute(\n   117\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   118\t                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n   119\t                (status, item_id),\n   120\t            ).rowcount == 1\n   121\t\n   122\t    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n   123\t        \"\"\"False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n   124\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   125\t            return conn.execute(\n   126\t                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1\n=== app/data_bites.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Data Bites: short, dated Markdown items.\n     2\t\n     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create, edit, publish, and unpublish any Data Bite\n     4\t(shift continuity, ADR-003); only a Director may delete one, which the routes\n     5\tenforce. Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n     6\t\n     7\tPublic-facing code reads Data Bites only through `list_published`, so a draft\n     8\tcannot leak through it.\n     9\t\"\"\"\n    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    11\t\n    12\timport sqlite3\n    13\t\n    14\tfrom app.content import ContentTable\n    15\t\n    16\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"data_bites\", \"Data Bite\")\n    17\t\n    18\tcreate = _TABLE.create\n    19\tget = _TABLE.get\n    20\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n    21\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n    22\tdelete = _TABLE.delete\n    23\t\n    24\t\n    25\tdef update(bite_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> bool:\n    26\t    \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. False if there is no such Data Bite.\"\"\"\n    27\t    return _TABLE.update(bite_id, title, slug, body)\n    28\t\n    29\t\n    30\tdef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    31\t    \"\"\"The public-facing query: published Data Bites only, newest first.\"\"\"\n    32\t    return _TABLE.list_published(\"c.created_at DESC, c.id DESC\")\n=== app/reports.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Reports: durable, cite-able Markdown documents (the Factbook, the CDS).\n     2\t\n     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create a Report (always as a draft) and edit a\n     4\tdraft one, whoever started it (shift continuity, ADR-003). Once a Report is\n     5\tpublished only a Director may change it: `update` enforces that in the same\n     6\tstatement that writes, and the routes make publish, unpublish, and delete\n     7\tDirector only. Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n     8\t\n     9\tA Report may carry one attached PDF (checked by app.uploads). Attaching,\n    10\treplacing, or removing it follows the same lockdown as the body. The file is\n    11\tstored under settings.UPLOADS, outside site/, named by the Report's id; the\n    12\t`file_name` column says whether there is one.\n    13\t\n    14\tPublic-facing code reads Reports only through `list_published`, so a draft\n    15\tcannot leak through it.\n    16\t\"\"\"\n    17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    18\t\n    19\timport os\n    20\timport sqlite3\n    21\timport tempfile\n    22\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    23\t\n    24\tfrom app import db, settings\n    25\tfrom app.content import AlsoWrite, ContentError, ContentTable\n    26\tfrom app.uploads import Pdf\n    27\tfrom app.users import is_director\n    28\t\n    29\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"reports\", \"Report\")\n    30\t\n    31\tget = _TABLE.get\n    32\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n    33\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n    34\t\n    35\t\n    36\tclass ReportLocked(ContentError):\n    37\t    \"\"\"A published Report, and the user is not a Director.\"\"\"\n    38\t\n    39\t\n    40\tdef can_edit(report: sqlite3.Row, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n    41\t    \"\"\"The lockdown rule. `update` and `remove_file` apply the same rule in\n    42\t    their UPDATEs.\"\"\"\n    43\t    return report[\"status\"] == \"draft\" or is_director(user)\n    44\t\n    45\t\n    46\tdef file_path(report_id: int) -> Path:\n    47\t    \"\"\"Where a Report's attached file is stored. Built from the id alone.\"\"\"\n    48\t    return settings.UPLOADS / \"reports\" / f\"{int(report_id)}.pdf\"\n    49\t\n    50\t\n    51\tdef _write_atomically(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:\n    52\t    \"\"\"Replace `path` in one step, so a failed write never leaves half a file.\"\"\"\n    53\t    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    54\t    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=\".part\")\n    55\t    try:\n    56\t        with os.fdopen(fd, \"wb\") as f:\n    57\t            f.write(data)\n    58\t        os.replace(tmp, path)\n    59\t    except BaseException:\n    60\t        Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n    61\t        raise\n    62\t\n    63\t\n    64\tdef _attaching(pdf: Pdf | None) -> AlsoWrite | None:\n    65\t    \"\"\"Attach `pdf` in the same transaction as the Report's row, so the body\n    66\t    and the file are saved together or not at all.\"\"\"\n    67\t    if pdf is None:\n    68\t        return None\n    69\t\n    70\t    def attach(conn: sqlite3.Connection, report_id: int) -> None:\n    71\t        conn.execute(\"UPDATE reports SET file_name = ? WHERE id = ?\", (pdf.name, report_id))\n    72\t        _write_atomically(file_path(report_id), pdf.data)\n    73\t\n    74\t    return attach\n    75\t\n    76\t\n    77\tdef _missing_or_locked(report_id: int) -> bool:\n    78\t    \"\"\"After a guarded write changed nothing: False if there is no such\n    79\t    Report, otherwise it was published and locked.\"\"\"\n    80\t    if get(report_id) is None:\n    81\t        return False\n    82\t    raise ReportLocked(\"Only the Director can change a published Report.\")\n    83\t\n    84\t\n    85\tdef create(title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n    86\t           pdf: Pdf | None = None) -> int:\n    87\t    \"\"\"Create a draft Report, with its file if one is given.\"\"\"\n    88\t    return _TABLE.create(title, slug, body, author_id, also=_attaching(pdf))\n    89\t\n    90\t\n    91\tdef update(report_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n    92\t           user: sqlite3.Row, pdf: Pdf | None = None) -> bool:\n    93\t    \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body on behalf of `user`, and attach or replace\n    94\t    the file if one is given. False if there is no such Report; ReportLocked if\n    95\t    it is published and `user` is not a Director.\"\"\"\n    96\t    if _TABLE.update(report_id, title, slug, body, drafts_only=not is_director(user),\n    97\t                     also=_attaching(pdf)):\n    98\t        return True\n    99\t    return _missing_or_locked(report_id)\n   100\t\n   101\t\n   102\tdef remove_file(report_id: int, *, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n   103\t    \"\"\"Remove the Report's file on behalf of `user`, as `update`.\"\"\"\n   104\t    with db.connect() as conn:\n   105\t        removed = conn.execute(\n   106\t            \"UPDATE reports SET file_name = NULL, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   107\t            \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR ?)\",\n   108\t            (report_id, is_director(user)),\n   109\t        ).rowcount == 1\n   110\t    if not removed:\n   111\t        return _missing_or_locked(report_id)\n   112\t    # Only once the row no longer names it, so a failed commit keeps the file.\n   113\t    file_path(report_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n   114\t    return True\n   115\t\n   116\t\n   117\tdef delete(report_id: int) -> bool:\n   118\t    \"\"\"Delete the Report and its file. False if there is no such Report.\"\"\"\n   119\t    if not _TABLE.delete(report_id):\n   120\t        return False\n   121\t    file_path(report_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n   122\t    return True\n   123\t\n   124\t\n   125\tdef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   126\t    \"\"\"The public-facing query: published Reports only, by title.\"\"\"\n   127\t    return _TABLE.list_published(\"c.title, c.id\")\n=== app/db.py\n     1\t\"\"\"SQLite access. Every table's schema lives here, so init_db() builds them all.\"\"\"\n     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     3\t\n     4\timport sqlite3\n     5\tfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n     6\tfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n     7\t\n     8\tfrom app import settings\n     9\t\n    10\tSCHEMA = \"\"\"\n    11\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    12\t    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    13\t    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    14\t    name          TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    15\t    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    16\t    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    17\t    is_active     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    18\t    created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n    19\t);\n    20\t\n    21\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data_bites (\n    22\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    23\t    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    24\t    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    25\t    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    26\t    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    27\t    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    28\t    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    29\t    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n    30\t);\n    31\t\n    32\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (\n    33\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    34\t    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    35\t    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- unique among Reports only; a Data Bite may share it\n    36\t    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n    37\t    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    38\t    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    39\t    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    40\t    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n    41\t    file_name  TEXT    -- the attached PDF's sanitized name for display; NULL if none\n    42\t);\n    43\t\"\"\"\n    44\t\n    45\t# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition).\n    46\t# CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves an existing table alone, so init_db adds\n    47\t# any of these an older database is missing.\n    48\tADDED_COLUMNS = [\n    49\t    (\"reports\", \"file_name\", \"TEXT\"),\n    50\t]\n    51\t\n    52\t\n    53\t@contextmanager\n    54\tdef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    55\t    \"\"\"Open the database named by settings (read at call time, so tests can swap\n    56\t    it). Commits on success, rolls back on error, always closes.\"\"\"\n    57\t    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    58\t    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    59\t    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    60\t    try:\n    61\t        with conn:\n    62\t            yield conn\n    63\t    finally:\n    64\t        conn.close()\n    65\t\n    66\t\n    67\tdef init_db() -> None:\n    68\t    with connect() as conn:\n    69\t        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n    70\t        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n    71\t            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n    72\t            if column not in existing:\n    73\t                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n=== app/main.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n     2\t\n     3\tThe admin console lives under /admin (login required) and the public preview\n     4\tat /. Routes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are included here.\n     5\tKeep this file small.\n     6\t\"\"\"\n     7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     8\t\n     9\timport sys\n    10\tfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\n    11\t\n    12\tfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request\n    13\tfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n    14\tfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n    15\t\n    16\tfrom app import db, settings\n    17\tfrom app.auth import LoginRequired, current_user\n    18\tfrom app.data_bites import list_published as published_data_bites\n    19\tfrom app.reports import list_published as published_reports\n    20\tfrom app.routes import admin, auth, data_bites, reports, users\n    21\tfrom app.templating import templates\n    22\t\n    23\tSESSION_MAX_AGE = 8 * 60 * 60  # one working day\n    24\tALL_METHODS = [\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"POST\", \"PUT\", \"PATCH\", \"DELETE\", \"OPTIONS\"]\n    25\t\n    26\t\n    27\t@asynccontextmanager\n    28\tasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n    29\t    # At server start, not import, so importing app.main never touches a database.\n    30\t    db.init_db()\n    31\t    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_PLACEHOLDER:\n    32\t        print(\"WARNING: CMS_SECRET_KEY is unset or the .env.example placeholder; \"\n    33\t              \"session cookies can be forged. Set a long random value in .env.\",\n    34\t              file=sys.stderr)\n    35\t    yield\n    36\t\n    37\t\n    38\tdef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    39\t    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", lifespan=lifespan)\n    40\t    app.add_middleware(\n    41\t        SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n    42\t        session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE, same_site=\"lax\",\n    43\t    )\n    44\t\n    45\t    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    46\t    def redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n    47\t        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n    48\t\n    49\t    @app.get(\"/\")\n    50\t    def public_home(request: Request):\n    51\t        # Titles only: the public pages (and links to them) arrive with the\n    52\t        # public-site ticket, T07.\n    53\t        data_bite_items = [{\"title\": b[\"title\"]} for b in published_data_bites()]\n    54\t        report_items = [{\"title\": r[\"title\"]} for r in published_reports()]\n    55\t        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n    56\t            request, \"public/home.html\",\n    57\t            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": data_bite_items,\n    58\t             \"reports\": report_items},\n    59\t        )\n    60\t\n    61\t    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    62\t    app.include_router(admin.router)\n    63\t    app.include_router(users.router)\n    64\t    app.include_router(data_bites.router)\n    65\t    app.include_router(reports.router)\n    66\t\n    67\t    # Must stay last: any /admin request no router above claimed, by path or by\n    68\t    # method. Anonymous visitors are sent to login (so they can't probe which\n    69\t    # admin paths exist); signed-in users get 405/404.\n    70\t    @app.api_route(\"/admin\", methods=ALL_METHODS,\n    71\t                   dependencies=[Depends(current_user)], include_in_schema=False)\n    72\t    def admin_method_not_allowed():\n    73\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=405)\n    74\t\n    75\t    @app.api_route(\"/admin/{rest:path}\", methods=ALL_METHODS,\n    76\t                   dependencies=[Depends(current_user)], include_in_schema=False)\n    77\t    def admin_not_found(rest: str):\n    78\t        if rest == \"\":\n    79\t            return RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=307)\n    80\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n    81\t\n    82\t    return app\n    83\t\n    84\t\n    85\tapp = create_app()\n=== app/templating.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The Jinja environment the admin console renders with.\"\"\"\n     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     3\t\n     4\tfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n     5\t\n     6\tfrom app import settings\n     7\tfrom app.auth import csrf_token\n     8\tfrom app.users import ROLE_LABELS\n     9\t\n    10\ttemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n    11\ttemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\n    12\ttemplates.env.filters[\"role_label\"] = ROLE_LABELS.get\n=== app/publish.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n     2\t\n     3\tT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\n     4\trender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n     5\t\n     6\t  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n     7\t  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     8\t     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n     9\t\"\"\"\n    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    11\t\n    12\timport shutil\n    13\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    14\t\n    15\tfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n    16\t\n    17\tfrom app import settings\n    18\t\n    19\tCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n    20\t:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n    21\tbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\n    22\theader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\n    23\tmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n    24\t\"\"\"\n    25\t\n    26\t\n    27\tdef environment() -> Environment:\n    28\t    return Environment(\n    29\t        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n    30\t        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    31\t    )\n    32\t\n    33\t\n    34\tdef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    35\t    out = out or settings.SITE\n    36\t    if out.exists():\n    37\t        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    38\t    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    39\t    env = environment()\n    40\t    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    41\t    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n    42\t        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n    43\t            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n    44\t            home_path=\"index.html\",\n    45\t        )\n    46\t    )\n    47\t    return out\n=== app/routes/admin.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The admin console. Every route on this router requires an active session:\n     2\tadd new admin routes here (or to a router built the same way) and they are\n     3\tprotected without further work.\"\"\"\n     4\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     5\t\n     6\tfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\n     7\t\n     8\tfrom app.auth import current_user\n     9\tfrom app.templating import templates\n    10\t\n    11\trouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin\", dependencies=[Depends(current_user)])\n    12\t\n    13\t\n    14\t@router.get(\"\")\n    15\tdef admin_home(request: Request, user=Depends(current_user)):\n    16\t    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n    17\t        request, \"admin/home.html\",\n    18\t        {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\", \"user\": user},\n    19\t    )\n=== app/routes/data_bites.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Data Bites in the admin console. AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n96\t    95\t                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n97\t    96\t                ).rowcount == 1\n98\t    97\t                if changed and also:\n99\t    98\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n100\t    99\t                return changed\n101\t   100\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n102\t   101\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n103\t   102\t\n104\t   103\t    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n105\t   104\t        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n106\t   105\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n107\t   106\t\n108\t   107\t    def list_all(self) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n109\t   108\t        return self._select(\"1\", \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\")\n110\t   109\t\n111\t   110\t    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n112\t   111\t        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n113\t   112\t\n114\t   113\t    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n115\t   114\t        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n116\t   115\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n117\t   116\t            return conn.execute(\n118\t   117\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n119\t   118\t                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n120\t   119\t                (status, item_id),\n121\t   120\t            ).rowcount == 1\n122\t   121\t\n123\t   122\t    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n124\t   123\t        \"\"\"False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n125\t   124\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n126\t   125\t            return conn.execute(\n127\t   126\t                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1\n128\t=== app/data_bites.py\n129\t     1\t\"\"\"Data Bites: short, dated Markdown items.\n130\t     2\t\n131\t     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create, edit, publish, and unpublish any Data Bite\n132\t     4\t(shift continuity, ADR-003); only a Director may delete one, which the routes\n133\t     5\tenforce. Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n134\t     6\t\n135\t     7\tPublic-facing code reads Data Bites only through `list_published`, so a draft\n136\t     8\tcannot leak through it.\n137\t     9\t\"\"\"\n138\t    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n139\t    11\t\n140\t    12\timport sqlite3\n141\t    13\t\n142\t    14\tfrom app.content import ContentTable\n143\t    15\t\n144\t    16\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"data_bites\", \"Data Bite\")\n145\t    17\t\n146\t    18\tcreate = _TABLE.create\n147\t    19\tget = _TABLE.get\n148\t    20\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n149\t    21\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n150\t    22\tdelete = _TABLE.delete\n151\t    23\t\n152\t    24\t\n153\t    25\tdef update(bite_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> bool:\n154\t    26\t    \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. False if there is no such Data Bite.\"\"\"\n155\t    27\t    return _TABLE.update(bite_id, title, slug, body)\n156\t    28\t\n157\t    29\t\n158\t    30\tdef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n159\t    31\t    \"\"\"The public-facing query: published Data Bites only, newest first.\"\"\"\n160\t    32\t    return _TABLE.list_published(\"c.created_at DESC, c.id DESC\")\n161\t=== app/reports.py\n162\t     1\t\"\"\"Reports: durable, cite-able Markdown documents (the Factbook, the CDS).\n163\t     2\t\n164\t     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create a Report (always as a draft) and edit a\n165\t     4\tdraft one, whoever started it (shift continuity, ADR-003). Once a Report is\n166\t     5\tpublished only a Director may change it: `update` enforces that in the same\n167\t     6\tstatement that writes, and the routes make publish, unpublish, and delete\n168\t     7\tDirector only. Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n169\t     8\t\n170\t     9\tA Report may carry one attached PDF (checked by app.uploads). Attaching,\n171\t    10\treplacing, or removing it follows the same lockdown as the body. The file is\n172\t    11\tstored under settings.UPLOADS, outside site/, named by the Report's id; the\n173\t    12\t`file_name` column says whether there is one.\n174\t    13\t\n175\t    14\tPublic-facing code reads Reports only through `list_published`, so a draft\n176\t    15\tcannot leak through it.\n177\t    16\t\"\"\"\n178\t    17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n179\t    18\t\n180\t    19\timport os\n181\t    20\timport sqlite3\n182\t    21\timport tempfile\n183\t    22\tfrom pathlib import Path\n184\t    23\t\n185\t    24\tfrom app import db, settings\n186\t    25\tfrom app.content import AlsoWrite, ContentError, ContentTable\n187\t    26\tfrom app.uploads import Pdf\n188\t    27\tfrom app.users import is_director\n189\t    28\t\n190\t    29\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"reports\", \"Report\")\n191\t    30\t\n192\t    31\tget = _TABLE.get\n193\t    32\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n194\t    33\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n195\t    34\t\n196\t    35\t\n197\t    36\tclass ReportLocked(ContentError):\n198\t    37\t    \"\"\"A published Report, and the user is not a Director.\"\"\"\n199\t    38\t\n200\t    39\t\n201\t    40\tdef can_edit(report: sqlite3.Row, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n202\t    41\t    \"\"\"The lockdown rule. `update` and `remove_file` apply the same rule in\n203\t    42\t    their UPDATEs.\"\"\"\n204\t    43\t    return report[\"status\"] == \"draft\" or is_director(user)\n205\t    44\t\n206\t    45\t\n207\t    46\tdef file_path(report_id: int) -> Path:\n208\t    47\t    \"\"\"Where a Report's attached file is stored. Built from the id alone.\"\"\"\n209\t    48\t    return settings.UPLOADS / \"reports\" / f\"{int(report_id)}.pdf\"\n210\t    49\t\n211\t    50\t\n212\t    51\tdef _write_atomically(path: Path, data: bytes) -> None:\n213\t    52\t    \"\"\"Replace `path` in one step, so a failed write never leaves half a file.\"\"\"\n214\t    53\t    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n215\t    54\t    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, suffix=\".part\")\n216\t    55\t    try:\n217\t    56\t        with os.fdopen(fd, \"wb\") as f:\n218\t    57\t            f.write(data)\n219\t    58\t        os.replace(tmp, path)\n220\t    59\t    except BaseException:\n221\t    60\t        Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n222\t    61\t        raise\n223\t    62\t\n224\t    63\t\n225\t    64\tdef _attaching(pdf: Pdf | None) -> AlsoWrite | None:\n226\t    65\t    \"\"\"Attach `pdf` in the same transaction as the Report's row, so the body\n227\t    66\t    and the file are saved together or not at all.\"\"\"\n228\t    67\t    if pdf is None:\n229\t    68\t        return None\n230\t    69\t\n231\t    70\t    def attach(conn: sqlite3.Connection, report_id: int) -> None:\n232\t    71\t        conn.execute(\"UPDATE reports SET file_name = ? WHERE id = ?\", (pdf.name, report_id))\n233\t    72\t        _write_atomically(file_path(report_id), pdf.data)\n234\t    73\t\n235\t    74\t    return attach\n236\t    75\t\n237\t    76\t\n238\t    77\tdef _missing_or_locked(report_id: int) -> bool:\n239\t    78\t    \"\"\"After a guarded write changed nothing: False if there is no such\n240\t    79\t    Report, otherwise it was published and locked.\"\"\"\n241\t    80\t    if get(report_id) is None:\n242\t    81\t        return False\n243\t    82\t    raise ReportLocked(\"Only the Director can change a published Report.\")\n244\t    83\t\n245\t    84\t\n246\t    85\tdef create(title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n247\t    86\t           pdf: Pdf | None = None) -> int:\n248\t    87\t    \"\"\"Create a draft Report, with its file if one is given.\"\"\"\n249\t    88\t    return _TABLE.create(title, slug, body, author_id, also=_attaching(pdf))\n250\t    89\t\n251\t    90\t\n252\t    91\tdef update(report_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n253\t    92\t           user: sqlite3.Row, pdf: Pdf | None = None) -> bool:\n254\t    93\t    \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body on behalf of `user`, and attach or replace\n255\t    94\t    the file if one is given. False if there is no such Report; ReportLocked if\n256\t    95\t    it is published and `user` is not a Director.\"\"\"\n257\t    96\t    if _TABLE.update(report_id, title, slug, body, drafts_only=not is_director(user),\n258\t    97\t                     also=_attaching(pdf)):\n259\t    98\t        return True\n260\t    99\t    return _missing_or_locked(report_id)\n261\t   100\t\n262\t   101\t\n263\t   102\tdef remove_file(report_id: int, *, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n264\t   103\t    \"\"\"Remove the Report's file on behalf of `user`, as `update`.\"\"\"\n265\t   104\t    with db.connect() as conn:\n266\t   105\t        removed = conn.execute(\n267\t   106\t            \"UPDATE reports SET file_name = NULL, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n268\t   107\t            \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR ?)\",\n269\t   108\t            (report_id, is_director(user)),\n270\t   109\t        ).rowcount == 1\n271\t   110\t    if not removed:\n272\t   111\t        return _missing_or_locked(report_id)\n273\t   112\t    # Only once the row no longer names it, so a failed commit keeps the file.\n274\t   113\t    file_path(report_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n275\t   114\t    return True\n276\t   115\t\n277\t   116\t\n278\t   117\tdef delete(report_id: int) -> bool:\n279\t   118\t    \"\"\"Delete the Report and its file. False if there is no such Report.\"\"\"\n280\t   119\t    if not _TABLE.delete(report_id):\n281\t   120\t        return False\n282\t   121\t    file_path(report_id).unlink(missing_ok=True)\n283\t   122\t    return True\n284\t   123\t\n285\t   124\t\n286\t   125\tdef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n287\t   126\t    \"\"\"The public-facing query: published Reports only, by title.\"\"\"\n288\t   127\t    return _TABLE.list_published(\"c.title, c.id\")\n289\t=== app/db.py\n290\t     1\t\"\"\"SQLite access. Every table's schema lives here, so init_db() builds them all.\"\"\"\n291\t     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n292\t     3\t\n293\t     4\timport sqlite3\n294\t     5\tfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n295\t     6\tfrom contextlib import contextmanager\n296\t     7\t\n297\t     8\tfrom app import settings\n298\t     9\t\n299\t    10\tSCHEMA = \"\"\"\n300\t    11\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n301\t    12\t    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n302\t    13\t    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n303\t    14\t    name          TEXT    NOT NULL,\n304\t    15\t    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n305\t    16\t    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n306\t    17\t    is_active     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n307\t    18\t    created_at    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n308\t    19\t);\n309\t    20\t\n310\t    21\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data_bites (\n311\t    22\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n312\t    23\t    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n313\t    24\t    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n314\t    25\t    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n315\t    26\t    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n316\t    27\t    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n317\t    28\t    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n318\t    29\t    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n319\t    30\t);\n320\t    31\t\n321\t    32\tCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reports (\n322\t    33\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n323\t    34\t    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n324\t    35\t    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,  -- unique among Reports only; a Data Bite may share it\n325\t    36\t    body       TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- raw Markdown; sanitized only when rendered\n326\t    37\t    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n327\t    38\t    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n328\t    39\t    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n329\t    40\t    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n330\t    41\t    file_name  TEXT    -- the attached PDF's sanitized name for display; NULL if none\n331\t    42\t);\n332\t    43\t\"\"\"\n333\t    44\t\n334\t    45\t# Columns added after a table was first created: (table, column, definition).\n335\t    46\t# CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS leaves an existing table alone, so init_db adds\n336\t    47\t# any of these an older database is missing.\n337\t    48\tADDED_COLUMNS = [\n338\t    49\t    (\"reports\", \"file_name\", \"TEXT\"),\n339\t    50\t]\n340\t    51\t\n341\t    52\t\n342\t    53\t@contextmanager\n343\t    54\tdef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n344\t    55\t    \"\"\"Open the database named by settings (read at call time, so tests can swap\n345\t    56\t    it). Commits on success, rolls back on error, always closes.\"\"\"\n346\t    57\t    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n347\t    58\t    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n348\t    59\t    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n349\t    60\t    try:\n350\t    61\t        with conn:\n351\t    62\t            yield conn\n352\t    63\t    finally:\n353\t    64\t        conn.close()\n354\t    65\t\n355\t    66\t\n356\t    67\tdef init_db() -> None:\n357\t    68\t    with connect() as conn:\n358\t    69\t        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n359\t    70\t        for table, column, definition in ADDED_COLUMNS:\n360\t    71\t            existing = {row[\"name\"] for row in conn.execute(f\"PRAGMA table_info({table})\")}\n361\t    72\t            if column not in existing:\n362\t    73\t                conn.execute(f\"ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {column} {definition}\")\n363\t=== app/main.py\n364\t     1\t\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n365\t     2\t\n366\t     3\tThe admin console lives under /admin (login required) and the public preview\n367\t     4\tat /. Routes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are included here.\n368\t     5\tKeep this file small.\n369\t     6\t\"\"\"\n370\t     7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n371\t     8\t\n372\t     9\timport sys\n373\t    10\tfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\n374\t    11\t\n375\t    12\tfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request\n376\t    13\tfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n377\t    14\tfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n378\t    15\t\n379\t    16\tfrom app import db, settings\n380\t    17\tfrom app.auth import LoginRequired, current_user\n381\t    18\tfrom app.data_bites import list_published as published_data_bites\n382\t    19\tfrom app.reports import list_published as published_reports\n383\t    20\tfrom app.routes import admin, auth, data_bites, reports, users\n384\t    21\tfrom app.templating import templates\n385\t    22\t\n386\t    23\tSESSION_MAX_AGE = 8 * 60 * 60  # one working day\n387\t    24\tALL_METHODS = [\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"POST\", \"PUT\", \"PATCH\", \"DELETE\", \"OPTIONS\"]\n388\t    25\t\n389\t    26\t\n390\t    27\t@asynccontextmanager\n391\t    28\tasync def lifespan(app: FastAPI):\n392\t    29\t    # At server start, not import, so importing app.main never touches a database.\n393\t    30\t    db.init_db()\n394\t    31\t    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_PLACEHOLDER:\n395\t    32\t        print(\"WARNING: CMS_SECRET_KEY is unset or the .env.example placeholder; \"\n396\t    33\t              \"session cookies can be forged. Set a long random value in .env.\",\n397\t    34\t              file=sys.stderr)\n398\t    35\t    yield\n399\t    36\t\n400\t    37\t\n401\t    38\tdef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n402\t    39\t    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", lifespan=lifespan)\n403\t    40\t    app.add_middleware(\n404\t    41\t        SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n405\t    42\t        session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE, same_site=\"lax\",\n406\t    43\t    )\n407\t    44\t\n408\t    45\t    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n409\t    46\t    def redirect_to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n410\t    47\t        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n411\t    48\t\n412\t    49\t    @app.get(\"/\")\n413\t    50\t    def public_home(request: Request):\n414\t    51\t        # Titles only: the public pages (and links to them) arrive with the\n415\t    52\t        # public-site ticket, T07.\n416\t    53\t        data_bite_items = [{\"title\": b[\"title\"]} for b in published_data_bites()]\n417\t    54\t        report_items = [{\"title\": r[\"title\"]} for r in published_reports()]\n418\t    55\t        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n419\t    56\t            request, \"public/home.html\",\n420\t    57\t            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": data_bite_items,\n421\t    58\t             \"reports\": report_items},\n422\t    59\t        )\n423\t    60\t\n424\t    61\t    app.include_router(auth.router)\n425\t    62\t    app.include_router(admin.router)\n426\t    63\t    app.include_router(users.router)\n427\t    64\t    app.include_router(data_bites.router)\n428\t    65\t    app.include_router(reports.router)\n429\t    66\t\n430\t    67\t    # Must stay last: any /admin request no router above claimed, by path or by\n431\t    68\t    # method. Anonymous visitors are sent to login (so they can't probe which\n432\t    69\t    # admin paths exist); signed-in users get 405/404.\n433\t    70\t    @app.api_route(\"/admin\", methods=ALL_METHODS,\n434\t    71\t                   dependencies=[Depends(current_user)], include_in_schema=False)\n435\t    72\t    def admin_method_not_allowed():\n436\t    73\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=405)\n437\t    74\t\n438\t    75\t    @app.api_route(\"/admin/{rest:path}\", methods=ALL_METHODS,\n439\t    76\t                   dependencies=[Depends(current_user)], include_in_schema=False)\n440\t    77\t    def admin_not_found(rest: str):\n441\t    78\t        if rest == \"\":\n442\t    79\t            return RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=307)\n443\t    80\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n444\t    81\t\n445\t    82\t    return app\n446\t    83\t\n447\t    84\t\n448\t    85\tapp = create_app()\n449\t=== app/templating.py\n450\t     1\t\"\"\"The Jinja environment the admin console renders with.\"\"\"\n451\t     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n452\t     3\t\n453\t     4\tfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n454\t     5\t\n455\t     6\tfrom app import settings\n456\t     7\tfrom app.auth import csrf_token\n457\t     8\tfrom app.users import ROLE_LABELS\n458\t     9\t\n459\t    10\ttemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n460\t    11\ttemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\n461\t    12\ttemplates.env.filters[\"role_label\"] = ROLE_LABELS.get\n462\t=== app/publish.py\n463\t     1\t\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n464\t     2\t\n465\t     3\tT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\n466\t     4\trender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n467\t     5\t\n468\t     6\t  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n469\t     7\t  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n470\t     8\t     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n471\t     9\t\"\"\"\n472\t    10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n473\t    11\t\n474\t    12\timport shutil\n475\t    13\tfrom pathlib import Path\n476\t    14\t\n477\t    15\tfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n478\t    16\t\n479\t    17\tfrom app import settings\n480\t    18\t\n481\t    19\tCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n482\t    20\t:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\n483\t    21\tbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\n484\t    22\theader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\n485\t    23\tmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n486\t    24\t\"\"\"\n487\t    25\t\n488\t    26\t\n489\t    27\tdef environment() -> Environment:\n490\t    28\t    return Environment(\n491\t    29\t        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n492\t    30\t        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n493\t    31\t    )\n494\t    32\t\n495\t    33\t\n496\t    34\tdef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n497\t    35\t    out = out or settings.SITE\n498\t    36\t    if out.exists():\n499\t    37\t        shutil.rmtree(out)\n500\t    38\t    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n501\t    39\t    env = environment()\n502\t    40\t    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n503\t    41\t    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n504\t    42\t        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n505\t    43\t            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n506\t    44\t            home_path=\"index.html\",\n507\t    45\t        )\n508\t    46\t    )\n509\t    47\t    return out\n510\t=== app/routes/admin.py\n511\t     1\t\"\"\"The admin console. Every route on this router requires an active session:\n512\t     2\tadd new admin routes here (or to a router built the same way) and they are\n513\t     3\tprotected without further work.\"\"\"\n514\t     4\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n515\t     5\t\n516\t     6\tfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\n517\t     7\t\n518\t     8\tfrom app.auth import current_user\n519\t     9\tfrom app.templating import templates\n520\t    10\t\n521\t    11\trouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin\", dependencies=[Depends(current_user)])\n522\t    12\t\n523\t    13\t\n524\t    14\t@router.get(\"\")\n525\t    15\tdef admin_home(request: Request, user=Depends(current_user)):\n526\t    16\t    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n527\t    17\t        request, \"admin/home.html\",\n528\t    18\t        {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\", \"user\": user},\n529\t    19\t    )\n530\t=== app/routes/data_bites.py\n531\t     1\t\"\"\"Data Bites in the admin console.
